faq.q: What is the easiest way to start a social post?
faq.a: Start from a product photo, or from a frame that already has a border. You can build a plainer square once that one is posted.

faq.q: What kind of social post tends to get attention?
faq.a: A clear product close-up, with the offer in the first line, is the post people reply to. A wider scene can be the next test.

faq.q: How often should a shop post?
faq.a: Three finished photos a week is enough if you can keep that pace when orders pile up. Answer the comments. That conversation is part of the post.
Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits, Pro is $35 for 300, and Premium is $63 for 600. Each image is 24 credits, shown before it runs. Plan details live on the pricing page.

faq.q: Where can I use the square file?
faq.a: The download is square, so it fits a lot of feed posts. In each ad tool, check that words are not cut off. It does not resize itself into a tall story or a wide banner.

faq.q: Can I put my headline on the image?
faq.a: Yes. Add a short headline on the image, or type that line in your ad editor when you want to set the price there.

faq.q: Can I make several scenes from one photo?
faq.a: Yes. Build different settings from the same product photo and compare them before you spend.

faq.q: Do I have to label the image as AI?
faq.a: Rules differ by app and country. Follow the label your ad account asks you to show. For a looser phone-shot look, see [casual phone-style product photos](page:tpl-ugc).

more_sections.h2: Finish the Post Without a Second App
more_sections.lead: One project can take a dark product shot through to the square you post.

items.d: Raising the light on a dark serum bottle makes the label readable in the square.

items.t: Room for a Sticker or a Line
items.d: The square can carry a small sticker or a short line you write, so the offer sits where you want it.
The retouch, the scene, and the square export all happen here, so the file is not bouncing between apps.

more_sections.h2: A Finished Look Without a Design Job
more_sections.lead: You can finish a square without a designer on staff. Start from the cutout and stop when the product looks right.

items.d: A candle photo can lose the mail and the counter around it. The candle is then free for a clean scene.

items.t: Add Light and a Soft Shadow
items.d: A soft shadow sits a headphone case on the surface after the cutout, so it stops looking like it floats.
A short word can sit beside a necklace, where the metal leaves open space, and still read at phone size.
A holiday frame already has the border and the empty spot. A granola pouch can go in that spot instead of a border built from nothing.

more_sections.h2: Describe the Scene, Keep the Product
more_sections.lead: The note only has to name the setting. The product in your upload is the part that stays.

items.d: Describe the room, the street, or the season, and get a background that fits the product.
The uploaded item is placed into the setting you described, instead of being redrawn from scratch.

items.t: A Model When It Should Be Worn
items.d: If the piece belongs on a body, dress a virtual model in a linen shirt and keep that photo next to the flat one.

definition.title: What Is an AI Ad Image Generator?
paras: An AI ad image generator turns a product photo into a square the feed can run. Reuse one scene and the shop stays recognizable from post to post.
When a holiday is the right moment, drop the product into a frame that already has the border, then add the offer in your own words.

reasons.lead: The person who writes the offer and the person who finishes the photo can share one file.

items.d: Send the square to the teammate who writes offers. They can open a scarf ad on a laptop while you still have the original on your phone.
Keep marks, colors, and layouts in one library so the next post matches the last.
The offer writer can leave a note on the design, and the change lands in the file before anyone downloads it.
